questions.question: Complete: If you (tune) in at seven o'clock, you will hear the news.
questions.answer: tune

questions.question: Complete: If I (have) a radio, I would listen to the farming programme.
questions.answer: had

questions.question: Complete: If I were you, I (not buy) that old player.
questions.answer: would not buy

questions.question: Complete: Sarah is a good presenter and so Doreen.
questions.answer: is

questions.question: Complete: Musa does not like adverts and does Peter.
questions.answer: neither

questions.question: Rewrite using needn't have: You switched off the television, but it was not necessary.
questions.answer: You needn't have switched off the television.

questions.question: Change to reported speech: "I am watching the news," said Father.
questions.answer: Father said that he was watching the news.

questions.question: Change to reported speech: "Connect the extension cable," the teacher told us.
questions.answer: The teacher told us to connect the extension cable.

questions.question: Give any four kinds of programmes broadcast on radio or television.
questions.answer: Any four of: news, sports, music, drama, documentaries, talk shows, farming programmes, children's programmes, religious programmes, adverts.

questions.question: What five questions must a good news item answer?
questions.answer: Who, what, when, where, why (and how).

questions.question: Write a short announcement (about three sentences) telling P.7 pupils about a briefing on Monday.
questions.answer: Learner's answer, for example: All P.7 pupils are informed that a briefing about the examinations will take place on Monday at 9:00 a.m. in the school hall. Every candidate must attend with a pen and a notebook. For more information, see the head teacher.

questions.question: Write a short advert (about three sentences) for a shop selling school bags.
questions.answer: Learner's answer, for example: Are you looking for a strong school bag? Visit Mukwano Bag Shop, opposite the market, for strong bags from only 25,000 shillings. Hurry while stocks last!

questions.question: Give any four advantages and four disadvantages of electronic media.
questions.answer: Advantages: fast information; learning and research; entertainment; communication over long distances (any four). Disadvantages: high cost of gadgets and data; bad content and time wasting; eye strain and little exercise; fraud; false news (any four).

questions.question: Give any five ways of caring for electronic gadgets.
questions.answer: Any five of: keep them dry and dust-free; hold discs by the edges; eject discs before switching off; keep away from strong sunlight and heat; switch off and unplug during storms; use the right cables and voltage; do not overload a socket; keep away from small children.

questions.question: Use I don't like and I like each in a sentence about programmes.
questions.answer: Learner's sentences, for example: I like watching the weather forecast. / I don't like long adverts.

questions.question: Give the difference between If 1 and If 2, with one example of each.
questions.answer: If 1 is about something real and likely and uses If + present simple, will + verb: If it rains, we shall stay indoors. If 2 is about something imagined or unlikely now and uses If + past simple, would + verb: If I had a television, I would watch the news.

questions.question: Write a short dialogue (six lines) between two friends discussing their favourite programmes.
questions.answer: Learner's dialogue. It should have two speakers named, a new line for each speaker, correct punctuation and natural language, for example: Ann: Which programme do you like most? Ben: I like the sports news. And you?

questions.question: Give the difference between a right and a responsibility, with one example of each.
questions.answer: A right is something a child is entitled to, for example the right to education; a responsibility is a duty the child is expected to perform, for example attending school regularly and doing homework.

questions.question: Name any five rights of a child and the responsibility that goes with each.
questions.answer: Any five pairs from the table, for example: the right to food — helping with the chores; the right to education — attending school regularly; the right to medical care — keeping clean and reporting illness; the right to play — playing safely; the right to protection — reporting abuse.

questions.question: Give the meaning of: child labour, dropout, early marriage, bad touches.
questions.answer: Child labour — making a child do heavy or harmful work; dropout — a learner who leaves school before finishing; early marriage — marrying while still a child; bad touches — touching a child's private parts or in a way that is not right.

questions.question: What should a child do if somebody tries to touch him or her wrongly?
questions.answer: The child should say NO loudly, get away from the person, and tell a trusted adult at once — a parent, teacher, religious leader, police officer or child helpline. The child must not keep it a secret, and it is never the child's fault.

questions.question: Complete: All children go to school. (two words)
questions.answer: ought to

questions.question: Complete: You should move in groups avoid child abuse. (three words)
questions.answer: in order to

questions.question: Complete: You provide food to your children you risk going to prison.
questions.answer: You either provide food to your children or you risk going to prison.

questions.question: Fill in the correct relative pronoun: The teacher helped the orphan was rewarded.
questions.answer: who

questions.question: Fill in the correct relative pronoun: The goat leg was broken has been treated.
questions.answer: whose

questions.question: Fill in the correct relative pronoun: This is the sanctuary the animals are kept.
questions.answer: where

questions.question: Rewrite in the future continuous: We shall discuss children's rights this time tomorrow.
questions.answer: This time tomorrow, we shall be discussing children's rights.

questions.question: Rewrite using the past perfect: The poacher escaped. Then the rangers arrived.
questions.answer: The poacher had escaped before the rangers arrived.

questions.question: Name the five freedoms of animals.
questions.answer: Freedom from hunger and thirst; freedom from discomfort; freedom from pain, injury and disease; freedom to express natural behaviour; freedom from fear and distress.

questions.question: Give any five ways in which people abuse animals.
questions.answer: Any five of: overloading and overworking; beating and stoning; tying legs tightly or hanging animals on bicycles; starving them or giving dirty water; keeping them in dirty, tight places; not treating sickness; poaching; burning bush; abandoning pets.

questions.question: Give any five ways of caring for animals.
questions.answer: Any five of: give clean water and enough feed; build a clean dry shelter; treat and vaccinate them; handle them gently; give them space; protect them from thieves and wild animals; report cruelty and poaching.

questions.question: Give the full meaning of: UWA, UWEC, WSPA, USPA, WCU.
questions.answer: UWA — Uganda Wildlife Authority; UWEC — Uganda Wildlife Education Centre; WSPA — World Society for the Protection of Animals; USPA — Uganda Society for the Protection of Animals; WCU — Wildlife Clubs of Uganda.

questions.question: Form nouns from these verbs: protect, behave, decide, educate, capture.
questions.answer: protect → protection; behave → behaviour; decide → decision; educate → education; capture → captivity (or capture).

questions.question: Rewrite using Much as: Although a cow is an animal, it also needs protection.
questions.answer: Much as a cow is an animal, it also needs protection.

questions.question: Rewrite using need not have: Obbo tied his goat on the motorcycle carrier, but it was not necessary.
questions.answer: Obbo need not have tied his goat on the motorcycle carrier.

questions.question: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) explaining why children should protect animals.
questions.answer: Learner's paragraph. It should be one paragraph with clear reasons, such as: animals also feel pain; they give us food, work and money; wild animals bring tourists and income; caring for animals shows kindness; the law protects them; and animals cannot speak for themselves.

questions.question: Give the meaning of: pollution, erosion, habitat, conservation.
questions.answer: Pollution — making air, water or land dirty and harmful; erosion — the wearing away and carrying off of soil; habitat — the natural home of a plant or animal; conservation — the protection of nature and its resources.

questions.question: Give the difference between flora and fauna.
questions.answer: Flora means all the plants of an area, while fauna means all the animals of an area.

questions.question: Give the two meanings of the word refuse and use each in a sentence.
questions.answer: As a noun it means rubbish: The refuse was collected on Monday. As a verb it means to say no: They refuse to pay the fine.

questions.question: Name any six activities that damage the environment.
questions.answer: Any six of: cutting down trees, bush burning, overgrazing, poor farming on slopes, draining swamps, dumping garbage, smoke from factories and vehicles, mining and quarrying, poaching, pouring waste into rivers.

questions.question: Give any five reasons why the environment should be protected.
questions.answer: Any five of: to keep reliable rainfall; to protect the soil; to keep air and water clean; to protect the habitats of plants and animals; to keep supplying raw materials, food and medicine; to prevent floods, drought and disease; to attract tourists; to leave enough for future generations.

questions.question: Name any six ways of protecting the environment.
questions.answer: Any six of: afforestation and reafforestation; terracing and contour ploughing; mulching and cover crops; crop rotation and manure; controlled grazing; proper waste disposal; protecting wetlands and river banks; using solar and biogas; making and obeying laws; educating people.

questions.question: Complete: We must protect our environment have rain.
questions.answer: to

questions.question: Complete: Our well was polluted, we did not have clean water.
questions.answer: so

questions.question: Rewrite beginning with Since: We shall have no rain because the forests have been cut.
questions.answer: Since the forests have been cut, we shall have no rain.

questions.question: Complete: If we don't build terraces, the soil (erode).
questions.answer: will erode

questions.question: Complete: If we (not cut) the trees, we would have had more rain.
questions.answer: had not cut

questions.question: Complete: Bush burning overgrazing cause degradation. (three words)
questions.answer: as well as

questions.question: Complete: The head teacher as well as the pupils (be) planting trees yesterday.
questions.answer: was

questions.question: Form abstract nouns from: beautiful, poor, strong, protect, conserve, free.
questions.answer: beautiful → beauty; poor → poverty; strong → strength; protect → protection; conserve → conservation; free → freedom.

questions.question: Rewrite using had to: It was necessary for us to build terraces to protect our soil.
questions.answer: We had to build terraces in order to protect our soil.

questions.question: Give any four ways of disposing of waste properly.
questions.answer: Any four of: using dustbins and waste baskets; digging a rubbish pit; composting food waste; burning dangerous waste in an incinerator; recycling plastic, paper and metal; taking waste to a proper dumping site.

questions.question: Write a short message of not more than fifteen words for a poster about tree planting.
questions.answer: Learner's message, for example: "Plant a tree today — save the rain for tomorrow."

questions.question: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) about the importance of protecting the environment.
questions.answer: Learner's paragraph. It should have a topic sentence, three or four supporting reasons in the present tense, correct punctuation and a closing sentence.

questions.question: Give the difference between If 1 and If 3, with one example of each.
questions.answer: If 1 is about something real and likely: If we plant trees, we will get more rain. If 3 is about something in the past that did not happen: If we had planted trees, we would have had more rain.

questions.question: Use each of these words in a sentence of your own: mulching, incinerator, degrade.
questions.answer: Learner's sentences, for example: Mulching keeps the soil moist during the dry season. / The hospital burns its waste in an incinerator. / Bush burning can degrade the land.

questions.question: Name the three types of marriage mentioned in the syllabus.
questions.answer: Cultural (customary) marriage, religious marriage and state (civil) marriage.

questions.question: Give the meaning of: introduction (kwanjula), bride price, best man, matron of honour.
questions.answer: Introduction (kwanjula) — the ceremony where the man is formally introduced to the girl's family; bride price — property or money given in a customary marriage; best man — the man who supports the bridegroom; matron of honour — the married woman who supports the bride.

questions.question: Give one word for: the bunch of flowers carried by a bride.
questions.answer: A bouquet.

questions.question: Arrange these wedding events in the correct order: reception, engagement, wedding service, introduction.
questions.answer: Engagement → introduction → wedding service → reception.

questions.question: Give one word for: a woman whose husband has died.
questions.answer: A widow.

questions.question: Give one word for: a person chosen to take the place of the dead person.
questions.answer: An heir (a female one is an heiress).

questions.question: Give the meaning of: condolences, mourner, shroud, cremate.
questions.answer: Condolences — words expressing sorrow to the bereaved; mourner — a person who attends a funeral to show sorrow; shroud — the cloth in which a body is wrapped; cremate — to burn a dead body to ashes.

questions.question: Fill in: Neither the bride nor the bridegroom (be) late.
questions.answer: was

questions.question: Fill in: Both the maid of honour and the best man (be) present.
questions.answer: were

questions.question: Rewrite using prefer: He likes a religious marriage more than a state one.
questions.answer: He prefers a religious marriage to a state one. (Also: He prefers having a religious marriage to having a state one.)

questions.question: Fill in the correct relative pronoun: The church they wedded is near the market.
questions.answer: where

questions.question: Fill in the correct relative pronoun: The woman was the bride is my aunt.
questions.answer: who

questions.question: Fill in the correct emphatic pronoun: The President attended the state funeral.
questions.answer: himself

questions.question: Fill in: mourners arrived early, so the service started late. (Few / A few)
questions.answer: Few

questions.question: Rewrite in the past perfect: The mourners left. Then the rain started.
questions.answer: The mourners had left before the rain started.

questions.question: Rewrite in the future perfect: They will complete the funeral rites by Sunday.
questions.answer: By Sunday, they will have completed the funeral rites.

questions.question: Rewrite beginning Despite the fact that: Although Abdul was a rich man, he was buried in two shrouds.
questions.answer: Despite the fact that Abdul was a rich man, he was buried in two shrouds.

questions.question: Form adjectives from: culture, religion, tradition, ceremony.
questions.answer: culture → cultural; religion → religious; tradition → traditional; ceremony → ceremonial.

questions.question: Write a short dialogue (six lines) between two people planning to attend a wedding.
questions.answer: Learner's dialogue. It should name two speakers, start a new line for each speaker, and use correct punctuation and natural language.

questions.question: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) describing a ceremony you have attended.
questions.answer: Learner's paragraph. It should be one paragraph in the past tense, saying what the ceremony was, where and when it took place, what happened in order, and how the writer felt.

questions.question: Define a finite set and give one example.
questions.answer: A finite set is a set whose members can be counted and come to an end, for example {1, 2, 3, 4}.

questions.question: Give one example of an infinite set.
questions.answer: The set of counting numbers {1, 2, 3, …} — any set that never ends is acceptable.

questions.question: List all the subsets of the set {p, q}.
How many subsets has a set with 6 members?
questions.answer: 2⁶ = 64 subsets.

questions.question: How many proper subsets has a set with 4 members?
questions.answer: 2⁴ − 1 = 16 − 1 = 15 proper subsets.

questions.question: Given n(A) = 18, n(B) = 14 and n(A ∩ B) = 6, find n(A ∪ B).
In a class of 50 pupils, 30 study French, 25 study German and 10 study both. How many study neither?
questions.answer: Study at least one = 30 + 25 − 10 = 45. Neither = 50 − 45 = 5 pupils.

questions.question: In a group of 45 farmers, 28 grow maize, 24 grow beans and 3 grow neither. How many grow both crops?
questions.answer: At least one crop = 45 − 3 = 42. Both = 28 + 24 − 42 = 10 farmers.

questions.question: A bag has 4 green and 6 yellow sweets. Find the probability of picking a green sweet.
A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.answer: Numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6 → 2 out of 6. P = 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.question: What is the probability of picking a vowel from the letters of the word MATHEMATICS?
questions.answer: MATHEMATICS has 11 letters; the vowels are A, E, A, I → 4. P = 4/11.

questions.question: Write down the members of the set of prime numbers less than 10, and state whether it is finite or infinite.
questions.answer: {2, 3, 5, 7} — it is a finite set with 4 members.

questions.question: If a set has 32 subsets, how many members has it?
questions.answer: 2ⁿ = 32, and 2⁵ = 32, so the set has 5 members.

questions.question: In a class of 40 pupils, 22 like posho only, 9 like both posho and rice, and 4 like neither. How many like rice altogether?
questions.answer: Pupils who like at least one = 40 − 4 = 36. Rice altogether = 36 − 22 = 14 pupils.

questions.question: A letter is chosen from the word UGANDA. Find the probability that it is the letter A.
questions.answer: UGANDA has 6 letters and the letter A appears 3 times. P = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.question: Write 37,405,206 in words.
questions.answer: Thirty-seven million, four hundred five thousand, two hundred six.

questions.question: Write in figures: Fifty-two million, seven hundred thousand, four hundred nine.
What is the value of 8 in 48,913,000?
questions.answer: 8 is in the millions place, so its value is 8 × 1,000,000 = 8,000,000.

questions.question: Write 1,984 in Roman numerals.
Change MMCDXLV to Hindu-Arabic numerals. (Take MM = 2000.)
Change XCVII to Hindu-Arabic numerals.
Change 1011₂ to base ten.
Change 342₅ to base ten.
Change 19₁₀ to base two.
Change 47₁₀ to base five.
Subtract: 1100₂ − 101₂.
Multiply: 110₂ × 11₂.
Which is bigger, 1111₂ or 21₅? Show your working.
Write the largest and the smallest 8-digit numbers.

items.subject: Mathematics
subtopics: 1. THE FOUR BASIC OPERATIONS AND THEIR PROPERTIES

questions.question: Name the property shown by 7 × (10 + 5) = 7 × 10 + 7 × 5.
questions.answer: The distributive property.

questions.question: Use a quick method to work out 25 × 36 × 4.
Expand 8,704 using indices.
Write the number shown by (5 × 10⁴) + (3 × 10²) + (7 × 10⁰).
Write 68,000,000 in standard form.
Write 9,400 in standard form.
Change 6.05 × 10⁵ to an ordinary number.
Write the prime factorisation of 180.
Find the GCF of 48 and 72 using prime factorisation.
questions.answer: 48 = 2⁴ × 3; 72 = 2³ × 3². Smallest powers: 2³ × 3 = 24

questions.question: Find the LCM of 12 and 18 using prime factorisation.
questions.answer: 12 = 2² × 3; 18 = 2 × 3². Biggest powers: 2² × 3² = 36

questions.question: Find √784 by prime factorisation.
Find √1024.
The area of a square plot is 441 m². Find the length of one side.
Use the distributive property to work out 12 × 98.
Which of these numbers is divisible by 3: 4,517 or 4,518? Show your working.
questions.answer: 4+5+1+7 = 17 (not divisible by 3); 4+5+1+8 = 18 (divisible by 3). So 4,518 is divisible by 3.

questions.question: Test whether 7,236 is divisible by 4.
questions.answer: The last two digits are 36, and 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Yes, it is divisible by 4.

questions.question: Test whether 51,840 is divisible by 6.
questions.answer: It ends in 0, so it is divisible by 2. Digit sum = 5+1+8+4+0 = 18, divisible by 3. Yes, it is divisible by 6.

questions.question: List all the prime numbers between 20 and 40.
List the first five composite numbers.
Write the first six triangular numbers.
Write the first five cubic numbers.
Find the next two terms: 5, 12, 19, 26, …
questions.answer: The rule is add 7 → 33, 40.

questions.question: Find the next two terms: 3, 6, 12, 24, …
questions.answer: The rule is multiply by 2 → 48, 96.

questions.question: Find the missing number: 1, 4, 9, __, 25, 36.
questions.answer: 16 (the square numbers).

questions.question: Find the 12th term of the sequence 4, 9, 14, 19, …
questions.answer: First term 4, common difference 5. 12th term = 4 + (12 − 1) × 5 = 4 + 55 = 59.

questions.question: Which number between 60 and 70 is both a square and a cubic number?
questions.answer: 64 — it is 8 × 8 and also 4 × 4 × 4.

questions.question: What is the 9th triangular number?
Find the next two terms: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, …
questions.answer: Add the two numbers before → 21, 34.

questions.question: A number is divisible by 9 and its digits add up to 27. Write any one such three-digit number.
questions.answer: Any three-digit number whose digits add to 27, for example 999 (9 + 9 + 9 = 27).

questions.question: Work out 2/5 + 1/3.
Work out 5/6 − 1/4.
Work out 3/4 ÷ 5/8.
Find 2/7 of 3,500 shillings.
Change 7/8 to a decimal and say whether it terminates or repeats.
questions.answer: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875 — it terminates.

questions.question: Change 0.45 to a fraction in its simplest form.
Round off 3.826471 to the nearest hundred thousandth.
Round off 15.4962 to the nearest hundredth.
Five pens cost 7,500 shillings. Find the cost of 8 pens.
questions.answer: 1 pen = 7,500 ÷ 5 = 1,500. 8 pens = 12,000 shillings

questions.question: Eight workers build a wall in 15 days. How long would 10 workers take?
questions.answer: Total work = 8 × 15 = 120 worker-days. 120 ÷ 10 = 12 days

questions.question: Share 36,000 shillings between two boys in the ratio 4 : 5.
questions.answer: Total shares = 9; one share = 4,000. Boys get 16,000 and 20,000 shillings.

questions.question: Find 35% of 6,000 shillings.
A pupil scored 42 out of 60. Express this as a percentage.
A bicycle bought at 150,000 shillings was sold at 180,000. Find the percentage profit.
After a discount of 10%, a bag costs 27,000 shillings. Find its marked price.
Define an integer and give two examples.
questions.answer: An integer is any whole number that is positive, negative or zero, for example −4 and +7.

questions.question: Arrange in ascending order: −3, 5, 0, −8, 2.
Work out (−7) + (−6).
Work out (−9) + 15.
Work out 6 − (−4).
Work out (−6) × 4.
Work out (−8) × (−5).
The temperature was −3 °C at night and rose by 9 degrees by noon. Find the noon temperature.
A trader had a debt of 15,000 shillings and then earned 40,000. Using integers, find his position.
questions.answer: −15,000 + 40,000 = +25,000 shillings (he is now 25,000 in credit).

questions.question: Work out 4 ⊕ 3 in mod 6.
questions.answer: 4 + 3 = 7; 7 ÷ 6 leaves remainder 1, so the answer is 1 (mod 6).

questions.question: Work out 2 ⊖ 5 in mod 7.
questions.answer: Counting back 5 from 2 in mod 7: 2 → 1 → 0 → 6 → 5 → 4, so the answer is 4 (mod 7).

questions.question: Work out 3 ⊗ 4 in mod 5.
questions.answer: 3 × 4 = 12; 12 ÷ 5 leaves remainder 2, so the answer is 2 (mod 5).

questions.question: It is 10 o'clock. What time will it be after 9 hours?
Today is Friday. What day will it be after 45 days?
questions.answer: 45 ÷ 7 = 6 remainder 3. Counting 3 days from Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday.

questions.question: What is the total of all the angles in a pie chart?
A pie chart shows 480 pupils. If 160 are in P.6, find the angle of the P.6 sector.
On a pie chart of 540 books, the history sector is 60°. How many history books are there?
A family budget of 900,000 shillings shows food 140°, rent 100°, fees 70° and the rest savings. Find the amount saved.
Find the mean of 12, 15, 18, 21, 24.
Find the median of 7, 3, 9, 11, 5.
questions.answer: In order: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 → median = 7

questions.question: Find the mode of 4, 6, 4, 8, 9, 4, 6.
questions.answer: 4 (it appears three times)

questions.question: Find the range of 23, 9, 45, 17, 31.
Find the median of 6, 10, 14, 18.
questions.answer: The two middle values are 10 and 14 → (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12

questions.question: The mean of four numbers is 25. Three of them are 20, 27 and 31. Find the fourth number.
A motorist covers 240 km in 4 hours. Find the average speed.
A cyclist rides at 15 km/h for 2½ hours. How far does he go?
Give the coordinates of a point 3 units to the left of the origin and 4 units up.
Plot P(2, 1), Q(6, 1) and R(6, 5). What kind of triangle is PQR?
questions.answer: It is a right-angled triangle (the angle at Q is 90°).

questions.question: A number is picked at random from 1 to 12. Find the probability that it is an even number.
questions.answer: Even numbers from 1 to 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 → 6 out of 12. P = 1/2

questions.question: Define parallel lines and skew lines.
questions.answer: Parallel lines are lines in the same plane that never meet and are always the same distance apart. Skew lines are lines in different planes that never meet and are not parallel.

questions.question: Name the four types of angles formed when a line crosses two parallel lines.
questions.answer: Vertically opposite angles, corresponding angles, alternate angles and co-interior (allied) angles.

questions.question: Two parallel lines are crossed by a line. One of the co-interior angles is 105°. Find the other.
Describe briefly how to construct an angle of 60°.
questions.answer: Draw a straight line. Put the compass point at one end and draw an arc cutting the line. Without changing the radius, put the point where the arc cuts the line and draw another arc cutting the first. Join the end of the line to the point where the arcs cross.

questions.question: How is an angle of 45° constructed?
questions.answer: First construct a right angle (90°), then bisect it.

questions.question: Find the sum of the interior angles of an octagon.
Find each interior angle of a regular hexagon.
questions.answer: Exterior = 360 ÷ 6 = 60°, so interior = 180 − 60 = 120°

questions.question: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 30°. Find the number of sides.
The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 1,080°. How many sides has it?
State any three properties of a rhombus.
questions.answer: All four sides are equal; opposite angles are equal; the diagonals cross at 90° (and opposite sides are parallel).

questions.question: Write N 25° E as a three-figure bearing.
Write S 45° W as a three-figure bearing.
The bearing of Q from P is 130°. Find the bearing of P from Q.
On a map with scale 1 : 100,000 two towns are 8.5 cm apart. Find the real distance in kilometres.
Find the sum of the exterior angles of a decagon.
questions.answer: 360° — the exterior angles of every polygon add up to 360°.

questions.question: Change 5:45 p.m. to the 24-hour clock.
Change 11:20 a.m. to the 24-hour clock.
Change 18:35 to the 12-hour clock.
Change 00:40 to the 12-hour clock.
How many minutes are there in 3½ hours?
Change 250 minutes to hours and minutes.
questions.answer: 250 ÷ 60 = 4 remainder 10 → 4 hours 10 minutes

questions.question: A bus left at 08:15 and arrived at 12:05. Find the duration of the journey.
questions.answer: 12:05 − 08:15 = 3 hours 50 minutes

questions.question: A lesson started at 10:40 and lasted 55 minutes. When did it end?
A journey lasted 6 hours 30 minutes and ended at 15:10. When did it start?
A night bus left at 21:45 and reached its destination at 05:30. How long was the journey?
questions.answer: 21:45 to midnight = 2 h 15 min; midnight to 05:30 = 5 h 30 min. Total = 7 hours 45 minutes

questions.question: Using the travel timetable above, how long does the bus stop at Mukono?
Using the same table, how long does the bus take between Kampala and Jinja, including the stop at Mukono?
questions.answer: 09:35 − 07:30 = 2 hours 5 minutes

questions.question: How many hours are there in a week?
A film started at 7:50 p.m. and ended at 10:05 p.m. How long was it?
questions.answer: 10:05 p.m. − 7:50 p.m. = 2 hours 15 minutes

questions.question: Write midnight and midday in the 24-hour clock.
questions.answer: Midnight = 00:00; midday = 12:00

questions.question: Change 4.2 km to metres.
Change 3,750 g to kilogrammes.
Change 5.5 litres to millilitres.
Find the perimeter of a rectangle 15 cm by 9 cm.
Find the circumference of a circle of radius 14 cm. (π = 22/7)
The circumference of a circle is 132 cm. Find its radius.
Find the area of a rectangle 18 m by 12 m.
Find the area of a triangle with base 16 cm and height 7 cm.
Find the area of a circle of diameter 28 cm.
questions.answer: Radius = 14 cm. Area = 22/7 × 14 × 14 = 616 cm²

questions.question: Find the area of a trapezium whose parallel sides are 12 cm and 8 cm and whose height is 6 cm.
Find the volume of a cuboid 8 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm.
Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 20 cm.
A tank measures 2 m by 1 m by 0.5 m. Find its capacity in litres.
questions.answer: Volume = 2 × 1 × 0.5 = 1 m³ = 1,000 litres

questions.question: A rectangular garden 30 m by 20 m has a path 1 m wide all round it inside the garden. Find the area of the path.
questions.answer: Inner rectangle = (30 − 2) × (20 − 2) = 28 × 18 = 504 m². Garden = 600 m². Path = 600 − 504 = 96 m²

questions.question: How many 500 ml bottles can be filled from 12 litres of juice?
Simplify 7a + 5a − 3a.
questions.answer: 9a

questions.question: Simplify 8x + 3y − 5x + 2y.
questions.answer: 3x + 5y

questions.question: Remove the brackets and simplify: 4(2m + 3) − 5.
Remove the brackets and simplify: 3(x + 2) + 2(x − 4).
If p = 4 and q = 6, find the value of 3p + 2q.
If a = 5, b = 2, find the value of a² − 3b.
Solve 4x + 7 = 31.
Solve 9y − 5 = 40.
Solve 3(n − 2) = 18.
Solve 6k + 4 = 2k + 20.
Solve x/5 − 2 = 3.
Solve the inequality 3x − 4 < 11.
Solve 2y + 5 ≥ 17 and write the solution set if y is a whole number less than 9.
questions.answer: 2y ≥ 12 → y ≥ 6. Solution set = {6, 7, 8}

questions.question: A number is doubled and 9 is added. The answer is 35. Find the number.
The length of a rectangle is 3 m more than its width. The perimeter is 26 m. Find the length and the width.
questions.answer: Let width = w, length = w + 3. 2(w + w + 3) = 26 → 4w + 6 = 26 → 4w = 20 → w = 5. Width 5 m, length 8 m (perimeter 2 × 13 = 26 ✓)

items.subject: Science
subtopics: 1. THE STRUCTURE OF THE HUMAN SKELETON

questions.question: What is a skeleton?
questions.answer: A skeleton is the framework of bones that supports the body and gives it shape.

questions.question: Name the two main parts of the human skeleton.
questions.answer: The axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton.

questions.question: Name any four bones found in the arm and hand.
questions.answer: Any four of: humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges.

questions.question: Name the longest bone and the smallest bone in the human body.
questions.answer: Longest — the femur; smallest — the stapes in the middle ear.

questions.question: Give the three types of joints according to movement, with one example of each.
questions.answer: Immovable — joints of the cranium; slightly movable — joints between the vertebrae; freely movable — the shoulder joint.

questions.question: Name the four types of freely movable joints.
questions.answer: Ball and socket, hinge, pivot and gliding.

questions.question: Give the difference between a ligament and a tendon.
questions.answer: A ligament joins bone to bone, while a tendon joins muscle to bone.

questions.question: Differentiate between voluntary and involuntary muscles.
questions.answer: Voluntary muscles are under our control, for example the arm muscles; involuntary muscles work on their own, for example the muscles of the stomach.

questions.question: Which muscles work together to bend and straighten the arm?
questions.answer: The biceps and the triceps. The biceps contracts to bend the arm, and the triceps contracts to straighten it.

questions.question: State any four functions of the muscular–skeletal system.
questions.answer: Any four of: support, giving shape, protection of organs, movement, production of blood cells, storage of minerals, attachment of muscles.

questions.question: Name the disease caused by lack of vitamin D and calcium in children and give one sign.
questions.answer: Rickets — the child has bent (bowed) legs and soft, weak bones.

questions.question: Name the four types of fractures.
questions.answer: Simple (closed), compound (open), greenstick and comminuted.

questions.question: Give the first aid you would give to a person with a fractured arm.
questions.answer: Keep the person calm and still, do not try to push the bone back, support the arm with a splint and a sling, control any bleeding, and take the person to a health worker immediately.

questions.question: Give three ways of keeping the muscular–skeletal system healthy.
questions.answer: Any three of: eat a balanced diet rich in calcium and protein, get vitamin D from morning sunshine, exercise regularly, rest enough, avoid accidents, immunise against polio, keep correct posture.

questions.question: State any three importances of correct posture.
questions.answer: Any three of: it keeps the backbone straight, it prevents back and neck pain, it allows the lungs to work properly, it prevents deformities, it makes a person look smart.

questions.question: Define electricity and name its two types.
questions.answer: Electricity is a form of energy caused by the movement of electrons. Its two types are static electricity and current electricity.

questions.question: Give any four sources of electricity used in Uganda.
questions.answer: Any four of: dry cells, hydro-electric power, solar panels, wind, generators, geothermal, thermal (fossil fuels), biogas.

questions.question: Give the difference between a conductor and an insulator, with one example of each.
questions.answer: A conductor allows electricity to pass through it, for example copper; an insulator does not, for example rubber.

questions.question: Draw and label a simple electric circuit. (Cell, switch, bulb and connecting wires.)
questions.answer: Learner's drawing. It should show a cell, connecting wires, a switch and a bulb forming a complete (closed) loop.

questions.question: Give two differences between a series circuit and a parallel circuit.
questions.answer: In a series circuit the bulbs are in one path, so if one blows all go off and the bulbs are dimmer. In a parallel circuit each bulb is on its own branch, so if one blows the others stay on and the bulbs are brighter.

questions.question: What is a short circuit, and give two of its causes?
questions.answer: A short circuit is when current finds a shorter path of very little resistance and flows without passing through the appliance. Causes: worn out or bare wires touching, water reaching the wires, overloading a socket, poor wiring.

questions.question: State any four safety precautions in handling electricity.
questions.answer: Any four of: never touch switches with wet hands; do not put metal objects in sockets; do not overload sockets; replace worn out wires; switch off the mains before repairs; keep children away from sockets; never touch fallen power lines.

questions.question: Give any four uses of electricity in a home.
questions.answer: Any four of: lighting, cooking, ironing, refrigeration, pumping water, running radios and televisions, charging phones, running computers.

questions.question: Name any four magnetic materials.
questions.answer: Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.

questions.question: Give the difference between natural and artificial magnets, with one example of each.
questions.answer: Natural magnets are found in the ground, for example lodestone; artificial magnets are made by people, for example a bar magnet.

questions.question: State the law of magnetism.
questions.answer: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.

questions.question: Describe how you would make a magnet by the stroking method.
questions.answer: Place the steel bar on a table. Take one pole of a strong magnet and stroke the bar from one end to the other, always in the same direction, lifting the magnet high at the end of each stroke. Repeat many times; the bar becomes a magnet.

questions.question: Give three ways in which a magnet can lose its magnetism.
questions.answer: Any three of: heating it strongly, hammering or dropping it repeatedly, passing alternating current through it, storing it carelessly.

questions.question: How are magnets properly stored?
questions.answer: Bar magnets are stored in pairs with unlike poles facing each other and soft iron keepers placed across the ends.

questions.question: Explain briefly how an electric bell works.
questions.answer: When the switch is pressed, current flows through the electromagnet, which attracts the soft iron armature so that the hammer hits the gong. This movement breaks the circuit, the electromagnet loses its magnetism and the spring pulls the armature back, closing the circuit again. The action repeats quickly, so the bell rings continuously.

items.subject: Science
subtopics: 6. ENERGY FROM WIND, THE SUN AND THE EARTH

questions.question: Define energy and name any four forms of energy.
questions.answer: Energy is the ability to do work. Forms: heat, light, sound, electrical, chemical, mechanical (any four).

questions.question: What is the main source of energy on earth?
questions.answer: The sun.

questions.question: Name three energy resources obtained from water.
questions.answer: Hydro-electric power, steam energy and tidal energy.

questions.question: Name the three fossil fuels.
questions.answer: Coal, petroleum (crude oil) and natural gas.

questions.question: Give two disadvantages of using fossil fuels.
questions.answer: They pollute the air and cause global warming; they are non-renewable and will get used up. (Also: mining and drilling damage the environment.)

questions.question: Name two energy resources obtained from plants.
questions.answer: Any two of: firewood, charcoal, biofuel (ethanol or biodiesel), biogas from plant waste, crop residues such as bagasse.

questions.question: What is biogas and how is it made?
questions.answer: Biogas is a gas produced when animal dung or other organic waste rots in a digester without air. The gas is piped away and burnt for cooking and lighting.

questions.question: Give three advantages of using biogas.
questions.answer: Any three of: it is cheap and renewable; it uses waste; the slurry left over is good manure; it reduces the cutting of trees; it burns cleanly without smoke.

questions.question: Give two ways in which animals provide energy.
questions.answer: Animals give muscle energy — oxen ploughing, donkeys carrying loads — and their dung is used to make biogas.

questions.question: Give the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy resources.
questions.answer: Renewable resources can be replaced or never run out, such as solar and wind; non-renewable resources get used up and cannot be replaced, such as coal and oil.

questions.question: Classify these as renewable or non-renewable: solar, coal, wind, natural gas.
questions.answer: Renewable: solar, wind. Non-renewable: coal, natural gas.

questions.question: Name three hydro-electric power stations in Uganda.
questions.answer: Any three of: Nalubaale, Kiira, Bujagali, Isimba, Karuma.

questions.question: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of hydro-electric power.
questions.answer: Advantages: it is renewable and it does not pollute the air (also cheap to run, and the dam stores water). Disadvantages: dams are very expensive to build and they may flood people's land (also affected by drought).

questions.question: State any four importances of energy resources.
questions.answer: Any four of: cooking and lighting, running industries, transport, pumping water, powering hospitals and schools, communication, creating jobs, farm work.

questions.question: Suggest four ways of conserving energy in your home or school.
questions.answer: Any four of: switch off lights and appliances not in use; use energy-saving bulbs and stoves; use solar or biogas instead of firewood; plant trees for firewood; cover pots while cooking; service vehicles regularly; walk or share transport for short journeys.

questions.question: What is a simple machine? Give two ways in which machines make work easier.
questions.answer: A simple machine is a device that makes work easier. It allows a small effort to move a big load, and it can change the direction of the force applied.

questions.question: Define effort, load and fulcrum.
questions.answer: Effort is the force applied to the machine; load is the weight or resistance the machine works against; fulcrum is the fixed point about which a lever turns.

questions.question: A load of 800 N is lifted by an effort of 200 N. Find the mechanical advantage.
A machine has a mechanical advantage of 6. What effort is needed to lift a load of 540 N?
questions.answer: Effort = 540 ÷ 6 = 90 N

questions.question: State the principle of moments.
questions.answer: Load × distance of the load from the fulcrum = effort × distance of the effort from the fulcrum.

questions.question: A load of 50 N is 3 m from the fulcrum. Find the effort acting 5 m from the fulcrum on the other side.
Name the three classes of levers and give one example of each.
questions.answer: First class — see-saw or scissors; second class — wheelbarrow; third class — fishing rod.

questions.question: Name the class of lever to which a pair of pliers belongs.
questions.answer: First class (the fulcrum is between the effort and the load).

questions.question: What is an inclined plane, and give two examples?
questions.answer: An inclined plane is a slanting surface used to raise a load. Examples: a ramp and a plank used to roll a drum onto a lorry (also staircases and zigzag hill roads).

questions.question: Give two examples each of a wedge and a screw.
questions.answer: Wedge: axe, knife (also panga, nail, chisel). Screw: bolt and nut, screw jack (also vice, corkscrew).

questions.question: Give the difference between a fixed pulley and a movable pulley.
questions.answer: A fixed pulley only changes the direction of the force, so the effort equals the load; a movable pulley reduces the effort needed, giving a mechanical advantage of about 2.

questions.question: Give three examples of a wheel and axle.
questions.answer: Any three of: steering wheel, door knob, bicycle wheel and pedals, windlass on a well, tap handle, screwdriver.

questions.question: Define friction and give three examples of friction in daily life.
questions.answer: Friction is the force that opposes movement between two surfaces in contact. Examples: brakes stopping a bicycle; shoes gripping the ground when walking; a match lighting when struck.

questions.question: Give three ways of increasing friction and three ways of reducing it.
questions.answer: Increase: make surfaces rougher; put treads on tyres and shoes; press the surfaces together more firmly. Reduce: lubricate with oil or grease; use ball bearings or rollers; polish surfaces or streamline the shape.

questions.question: Give two disadvantages of friction.
questions.answer: It wears out tyres, shoes and machine parts, and it wastes energy as heat, so machines use more fuel. (It also causes noise and overheating.)

items.subject: Science
subtopics: 5. GOOD HABITS FOR THE WHOLE SYSTEM

questions.question: Define excretion and give the difference between excretion and egestion.
questions.answer: Excretion is the removal of waste products made inside the body. Egestion is the removal of undigested food (faeces), which was never part of the body's chemical processes.

questions.question: Name the four excretory organs and the waste each one removes.
questions.answer: Skin — sweat; kidneys — urine; lungs — carbon dioxide and water vapour; liver — bile pigments (and it makes urea).

questions.question: Name the two main layers of the human skin.
questions.answer: The epidermis and the dermis.

questions.question: Name any four parts found in the dermis.
questions.answer: Any four of: sweat glands, sebaceous glands, hair follicles, blood vessels, nerve endings, fatty layer.

questions.question: State any four functions of the skin.
questions.answer: Any four of: excretion of sweat, control of body temperature, protection against germs and injury, sensation, formation of vitamin D, storage of fat and water.

questions.question: Name any three skin diseases and the cause of each.
questions.answer: Any three, for example: scabies — mites; ringworm — a fungus; boils — bacteria; athlete's foot — a fungus; eczema — allergy or irritation.

questions.question: Give four ways of caring for the skin.
questions.answer: Any four of: bathe daily with soap and clean water; wear clean clothes; cut nails short; treat wounds early; eat a balanced diet and drink water; avoid sharing towels and combs; wear shoes.

questions.question: Name the four parts of the urinary system in the order urine passes through them.
questions.answer: Kidneys → ureters → urinary bladder → urethra.

questions.question: Name any three parts of a kidney.
questions.answer: Any three of: cortex, medulla, pelvis, nephrons, renal artery, renal vein.

questions.question: State any three functions of the kidney.
questions.answer: Any three of: filtering the blood, removing urea and excess salts, forming urine, controlling the amount of water in the body.

questions.question: Name any three diseases or disorders of the kidney.
questions.answer: Any three of: kidney stones, nephritis, kidney failure, bilharzia, cystitis.

questions.question: How is kidney failure treated?
questions.answer: By dialysis — cleaning the blood using a machine — or by a kidney transplant.

questions.question: Which two wastes do the lungs remove?
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide and water vapour.

questions.question: Name any three diseases of the lungs and give one way of preventing lung disease.
questions.answer: Any three of: tuberculosis, pneumonia, bronchitis, asthma, lung cancer, whooping cough. Prevention: do not smoke, keep rooms well ventilated, avoid smoke and dust, and immunise children.

questions.question: Give any four good habits that keep the excretory system working well.
questions.answer: Any four of: drink plenty of clean water; eat a balanced diet with little salt; bathe daily; exercise regularly; avoid alcohol, smoking and drug abuse; do not hold urine too long; go for medical check-ups.

items.subject: Science
subtopics: 1. LIGHT AS A FORM OF ENERGY
2. EFFECT OF DIFFERENT MATERIALS ON LIGHT

questions.question: Define light and give two natural and two artificial sources of light.
questions.answer: Light is a form of energy that enables us to see. Natural: the sun, lightning (also stars, fireflies). Artificial: electric bulb, candle (also torch, lantern).

questions.question: Give the difference between a luminous and a non-luminous body.
questions.answer: A luminous body produces its own light, for example the sun; a non-luminous body does not produce light but is seen when light falls on it, for example the moon.

questions.question: How does light travel? Describe one experiment that proves it.
questions.answer: Light travels in straight lines. Take three cards with holes punched at the same height, line them up with a candle behind them; the candle is seen only when the three holes are in a straight line. When one card is moved, the light is blocked.

questions.question: Give the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials, with one example of each.
questions.answer: Transparent lets nearly all light through (clear glass); translucent lets only some light through (frosted glass or oiled paper); opaque lets no light through (wood).

questions.question: What three things are needed for a shadow to form?
questions.answer: A source of light, an opaque object and a screen.

questions.question: Give the difference between a solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse.
questions.answer: In a solar eclipse the moon comes between the sun and the earth. In a lunar eclipse the earth comes between the sun and the moon.

questions.question: Describe the image formed by a pin-hole camera.
questions.answer: It is real, inverted (upside down), laterally inverted and smaller than the object.

questions.question: State the two laws of reflection.
questions.answer: (i) The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. (ii) The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same plane.

questions.question: Give four characteristics of an image formed by a plane mirror.
questions.answer: It is virtual, upright, the same size as the object, laterally inverted, and as far behind the mirror as the object is in front (any four).

questions.question: How does a periscope work?
questions.answer: It has two plane mirrors fixed at 45° facing each other. Light from the object strikes the top mirror and is reflected down to the lower mirror, which reflects it into the eye of the observer.

questions.question: What is refraction? Give three of its effects.
questions.answer: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one transparent material to another. Effects: a stick in water looks bent; a pool looks shallower than it is; a coin in water appears raised; dispersion and the rainbow (any three).

questions.question: Name the seven colours of white light in order.
questions.answer: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

questions.question: Name the two types of lenses and give one use of each.
questions.answer: Convex (converging) — used in a magnifying glass and cameras; concave (diverging) — used in spectacles for short sight.

questions.question: Name any five parts of the human eye and give the work of each.
questions.answer: Any five, for example: cornea — lets light in and starts bending it; iris — controls the size of the pupil; pupil — lets light into the eye; lens — focuses light on the retina; retina — where the image is formed; optic nerve — carries the message to the brain.

questions.question: Name two eye defects and how each is corrected.
questions.answer: Short sight is corrected with concave lenses; long sight is corrected with convex lenses.

items.subject: Science
items.topic: Interdependence of Things in the Environment
subtopics: 3. INTERDEPENDENCE OF LIVING AND NON-LIVING THINGS
5. MANAGING A SCHOOL OR HOME WOOD PROJECT

questions.question: Define the environment and name its two components.
questions.answer: The environment is everything that surrounds a living thing. Its components are the living (biotic) and the non-living (abiotic).

questions.question: Give three ways in which animals depend on plants.
questions.answer: Any three of: plants give animals food; plants give out oxygen; plants provide shelter and nesting materials; plants provide medicine and shade.

questions.question: Give three ways in which plants depend on animals.
questions.answer: Any three of: animals give out carbon dioxide used in photosynthesis; animal droppings and dead bodies make the soil fertile; animals pollinate flowers; animals disperse seeds; people plant and protect crops; burrowing animals aerate the soil.

questions.question: Give two ways in which plants depend on other plants.
questions.answer: Big trees give shade and shelter to smaller plants; climbing plants use others for support; fallen leaves rot into humus that feeds other plants; legumes add nitrogen to the soil (any two).

questions.question: Write down a food chain with four members.
questions.answer: For example: grass → grasshopper → lizard → hawk.

questions.question: What is a producer? What is a decomposer?
questions.answer: A producer is a green plant that makes its own food. A decomposer is an organism such as bacteria or fungi that rots dead matter and returns nutrients to the soil.

questions.question: Give the difference between a food chain and a food web.
questions.answer: A food chain shows one single path of food energy, while a food web is many food chains joined together, showing that animals feed on more than one thing.

questions.question: Give three ways in which plants depend on non-living things.
questions.answer: Plants use soil for anchorage and mineral salts, water for photosynthesis and transport, air for carbon dioxide, and sunlight as the energy for photosynthesis (any three).

questions.question: Give two ways in which non-living things benefit from living things.
questions.answer: Dead plants and animals add humus and make the soil fertile; plant roots hold the soil and prevent erosion; plants release oxygen and water vapour into the air (any two).

questions.question: Define agroforestry and name its three types.
questions.answer: Agroforestry is the growing of trees together with crops and/or animals on the same piece of land. Types: agri-silviculture, silvo-pastoral and agro-silvo-pastoral.

questions.question: State any five importances of agroforestry.
questions.answer: Any five of: provides firewood, timber and poles; gives shade and windbreaks; leaves make manure; roots control soil erosion; legumes add nitrogen; provides fodder, fruits and medicine; brings extra income; attracts rainfall; uses land productively.

questions.question: Give three ways of caring for trees on an agroforestry farm.
questions.answer: Any three of: watering seedlings, weeding and mulching, pruning branches, fencing against animals, applying manure, controlling pests and diseases, thinning.

questions.question: Give the difference between pollarding and coppicing.
questions.answer: Pollarding is cutting off the top branches and leaving the trunk standing, while coppicing is cutting the whole tree close to the ground so that new shoots grow from the stump.

questions.question: Outline any five steps in managing a school wood project.
questions.answer: Any five of: choose a suitable site; prepare a nursery bed and sow seeds; prepare the land and mark the spacing; transplant at the start of the rains; water and mulch; weed regularly; fence and protect from fire and animals; prune and thin; control pests; keep records; harvest properly and replant.

questions.question: Give three benefits of a school wood project.
questions.answer: Any three of: it supplies firewood and poles for the school; it teaches learners practical skills; it earns the school money; it gives shade and beautifies the compound; it protects the soil and the environment.

items.subject: Science
subtopics: 2. COMMUNITY HEALTH AND SOCIAL PROBLEMS AMONG YOUNG PEOPLE
4. INFORMATION AND DATA ON HUMAN POPULATION

questions.question: Name any five common sicknesses in a home and give the cause of each.
questions.answer: Any five, for example: malaria — a parasite carried by the mosquito; diarrhoea — germs in dirty food and water; typhoid — bacteria in contaminated food or water; worms — worm eggs from dirty hands or bare feet; cough and flu — viruses; scabies — mites.

questions.question: How is malaria spread and how can it be prevented at home?
questions.answer: Malaria is spread by the bite of an infected female anopheles mosquito. It is prevented by sleeping under a treated mosquito net, draining stagnant water, clearing bushes around the house, closing windows early, and getting tested and treated early.

questions.question: Give four ways of controlling common sicknesses in a home.
questions.answer: Any four of: keep the home clean; use a latrine and wash hands with soap; boil or treat drinking water; cover food; sleep under a treated net; immunise children; eat a balanced diet; go to a health centre early.

questions.question: Name any four health and social problems facing young people today.
questions.answer: Any four of: early pregnancy and early marriage, drug and substance abuse, HIV/AIDS and other STIs, defilement and sexual abuse, poor hygiene, child labour, peer pressure, poor nutrition.

questions.question: What is anti-social behaviour? Give four examples.
questions.answer: Anti-social behaviour is behaviour that harms other people or the community. Examples: stealing, bullying, drug abuse, vandalism, fighting, truancy, gambling (any four).

questions.question: Give three effects of drug abuse on a young person.
questions.answer: Any three of: poor health and addiction; poor performance and dropping out of school; involvement in crime and accidents; loss of money; broken relationships with family and friends.

questions.question: Give three ways of preventing anti-social behaviour among young people.
questions.answer: Any three of: guidance and counselling; using free time well in sports and clubs; choosing friends wisely and resisting peer pressure; obeying school and community rules; religious and moral teaching; reporting wrongdoing.

questions.question: What should a child do if an adult tries to touch his or her private parts?
questions.answer: The child should say NO firmly, get away from the person, and tell a trusted adult at once — a parent, teacher, health worker, religious leader or the police. The child should not keep it secret; it is never the child's fault.

questions.question: What is a health survey? Give four steps followed in carrying one out.
questions.answer: A health survey is the collecting of information about the health problems of a community so that they can be solved. Steps: choose the problem; prepare questions or a checklist; get permission from leaders; visit homes and record observations; organise the findings in tables or graphs; report to the community and health workers; suggest and take action (any four).

questions.question: Give three activities, other than a survey, used to address health concerns in a community.
questions.answer: Any three of: health education talks and radio programmes; immunisation campaigns; clean-up days; digging latrines and rubbish pits; protecting water sources; distributing mosquito nets; guidance and counselling.

questions.question: Define population and census.
questions.answer: Population is the total number of people living in a place at a particular time. A census is the official counting of all the people in a country.

questions.question: Give three ways of collecting information about the population.
questions.answer: Any three of: a national census; birth and death registers; health centre records; school registers; surveys and questionnaires; local council records.

questions.question: Give four reasons why a country needs population information.
questions.answer: Any four of: to plan for schools, hospitals, water and roads; to know the population growth rate; to plan for food and jobs; to share government services and funds fairly; to plan immunisation and other health services.

questions.question: Give four problems caused by a rapidly growing population.
questions.answer: Any four of: overcrowding and slums; pressure on schools, hospitals and water; unemployment and poverty; food shortage; land shortage and conflicts; destruction of forests and wetlands; fast spread of disease.

questions.question: Name any five activities of a school health club.
questions.answer: Any five of: cleaning the compound and latrines; checking personal hygiene; running hand-washing points; making health posters; performing drama, songs and poems; inviting health workers to give talks; growing vegetables and fruit; carrying out health surveys; keeping a first-aid box.

items.subject: Social Studies
items.topic: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
subtopics: 1. POSITION OF AFRICA USING LINES OF LATITUDE AND LONGITUDE
2. CONTINENTS OF THE WORLD AND THEIR SIZES
6. ISLANDS WHICH ARE PART OF AFRICA

questions.question: A continent
questions.answer: A continent is a very large mass of land on the earth's surface.

questions.question: A line of latitude
questions.answer: A line of latitude is an imaginary line running east to west, showing how far a place is north or south of the Equator.

questions.question: An island
questions.answer: An island is a piece of land completely surrounded by water.

questions.question: A capital city
questions.answer: A capital city is the city where the government of a country is based.

questions.question: The two largest continents in the world.
questions.answer: Asia and Africa.

questions.question: The four oceans of the world.
questions.answer: Atlantic Ocean, Pacific Ocean, Indian Ocean and Arctic Ocean.

questions.question: The six regions of Africa.
questions.answer: Northern Africa, West Africa, East Africa, Central Africa, Southern Africa and the Horn of Africa.

questions.question: Any three island countries of Africa.
questions.answer: Any three of: Madagascar, Seychelles, Mauritius, Comoros, Cape Verde, São Tomé and Príncipe.

questions.question: The four countries of the Horn of Africa.
questions.answer: Ethiopia, Somalia, Djibouti and Eritrea.

questions.question: The line of latitude that divides the earth into two equal halves.
questions.answer: The Equator.

questions.question: The ocean found to the west of Africa.
questions.answer: The Atlantic Ocean.

questions.question: The sea that separates Africa from Europe.
questions.answer: The Mediterranean Sea.

questions.question: The largest island in Africa.
questions.answer: Madagascar.

questions.question: The region of Africa in which Uganda is found.
questions.answer: East Africa.

questions.question: Why is Africa described as the only continent crossed by the Equator, both Tropics and the Prime Meridian?
questions.answer: Because Africa stretches from about 37°N to about 35°S and from about 17°W to about 51°E. This spread means the Equator crosses its middle, the Tropic of Cancer crosses the north, the Tropic of Capricorn crosses the south, and the Prime Meridian passes through West Africa. No other continent is crossed by all four.

questions.question: Why are lines of latitude and longitude important on a map?
questions.answer: They help us find the exact position of a place on a map. Latitude gives the distance north or south of the Equator, and longitude gives the distance east or west of the Prime Meridian. Where the two lines cross is the position of the place.

questions.question: A ship sails from Mombasa in Kenya to Lagos in Nigeria. Name the ocean it starts from and the ocean it ends in.
questions.answer: It starts in the Indian Ocean (Mombasa is on the east coast) and ends in the Atlantic Ocean (Lagos is on the west coast).

questions.question: Draw an outline map of Africa. On it, mark and label the Equator, the Tropic of Cancer and Uganda.
questions.answer: Learner's map. It should show an outline of Africa with a horizontal line through the middle labelled Equator, a horizontal line north of it labelled Tropic of Cancer, and Uganda marked in East Africa on the Equator.

questions.question: Give one reason why Tanzania's capital is Dodoma and not Dar es Salaam, its largest city.
questions.answer: Dodoma was chosen as the capital because it lies in the centre of the country, which makes it easier to reach from all parts of Tanzania. Dar es Salaam remains the largest city and main port.

questions.question: Kampala is at about 0° latitude. What does this tell you about Uganda's position on the earth?
questions.answer: It shows that Uganda lies on the Equator, so part of the country is in the Northern Hemisphere and part is in the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.question: Physical features
questions.answer: Physical features are the land forms that exist on the earth's surface and give the land its shape.

questions.question: A plateau
questions.answer: A plateau is a large area of fairly flat land raised high above the land around it.

questions.question: A delta
questions.answer: A delta is the fan-shaped area of flat land formed where a river deposits soil as it enters a lake or a sea through several channels.

questions.question: A rift valley
questions.answer: A rift valley is a long, deep, steep-sided valley formed when the land between two parallel faults sinks.

questions.question: Any three fold mountains or ranges in Africa.
questions.answer: Atlas Mountains, Cape Ranges, and the folded ridges of the Atlas system in Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

questions.question: Any three volcanic mountains in Africa.
questions.answer: Any three of: Mt Kilimanjaro, Mt Cameroon, Mt Elgon, Mt Kenya, Tibesti, Ahaggar.

questions.question: The three deserts of Africa named in this topic.
questions.answer: The Sahara Desert, the Kalahari Desert and the Namib Desert.

questions.question: Any four man-made lakes in Africa and the dams that formed them.
questions.answer: Lake Nasser — Aswan High Dam; Lake Volta — Akosombo Dam; Lake Kariba — Kariba Dam; Lake Kainji — Kainji Dam.

questions.question: The longest river in Africa.
questions.answer: The River Nile.

questions.question: The deepest lake in Africa.
questions.answer: Lake Tanganyika.

questions.question: The river on which Victoria Falls is found.
questions.answer: The River Zambezi.

questions.question: The sea into which the River Nile pours its water.
questions.answer: The Mediterranean Sea.

questions.question: The largest lake in Africa.
questions.answer: Lake Victoria.

questions.question: How are fault-block mountains formed?
questions.answer: The land cracks along two parallel faults. The block of land between the cracks is pushed upwards, or the land on either side sinks, leaving the middle block standing high as a mountain.

questions.question: Give two reasons why the water level of Lake Chad has been falling.
questions.answer: Long droughts with little rainfall, and too much water being taken from the rivers that feed it for irrigation. (Also: silting and the growth of the population around it.)

questions.question: Why do many rivers in Africa have waterfalls and rapids?
questions.answer: Because most of Africa is a plateau. Where a river leaves the high plateau and drops towards the coast, the sudden fall in the land makes waterfalls and rapids.

questions.question: A trader wants to send goods by water from Kinshasa to Europe. Name the river and the ocean the goods will pass through.
questions.answer: The River Congo, then the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.question: Give two ways in which mountains help the people who live near them, and one way they make life difficult.
questions.answer: Help: they receive relief rainfall for farming, have fertile volcanic soils, attract tourists, and are sources of rivers. Difficulty: they make the building of roads and railways hard and expensive (steep slopes also cause soil erosion and landslides).

questions.question: Why is the Namib Desert dry although it lies along the coast?
questions.answer: Because the cold Benguela ocean current flows along that coast. Air passing over cold water carries little moisture, so very little rain falls on the land.

questions.question: Draw the map of Africa and mark on it the River Niger, Lake Chad and the Atlas Mountains.
questions.answer: Learner's map. The Niger should be shown in West Africa flowing into the Gulf of Guinea, Lake Chad in the middle of West/Central Africa, and the Atlas Mountains in the far north-west.

items.subject: Social Studies
subtopics: 3. FACTORS THAT INFLUENCE THE CLIMATE OF AFRICA
5. INFLUENCE OF CLIMATE ON HUMAN ACTIVITIES
6. INFLUENCE OF HUMAN ACTIVITIES ON CLIMATE

questions.question: Weather
questions.answer: Weather is the condition of the atmosphere of a place at a particular time.

questions.question: Climate
questions.answer: Climate is the average weather conditions of a place recorded over a long period of time.

questions.question: Desertification
questions.answer: Desertification is the spread of desert conditions into land that was not desert before.

questions.question: A rain shadow
questions.answer: A rain shadow is the dry leeward side of a mountain, which receives little rainfall because the moist air lost its water on the windward side.

questions.question: Any four elements of weather and the instrument used to measure each.
questions.answer: Rainfall — rain gauge; temperature — thermometer; wind direction — wind vane; wind speed — anemometer. (Also humidity — hygrometer; air pressure — barometer.)

questions.question: The six climatic regions of Africa.
questions.answer: Equatorial, Tropical (savannah), Desert, Mediterranean, Temperate and Montane.

questions.question: The three hot deserts of Africa.
questions.answer: The Sahara, the Kalahari and the Namib.

questions.question: Any three factors that influence the climate of Africa.
questions.answer: Any three of: latitude, altitude, nearness to water bodies, winds, ocean currents, relief, vegetation, human activities, land mass.

questions.question: The type of climate that has hot dry summers and warm wet winters.
questions.answer: The Mediterranean climate.

questions.question: One country in Africa with a Mediterranean climate.
questions.answer: Any one of: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt or South Africa.

questions.question: The ocean current that makes the Namib Desert dry.
questions.answer: The cold Benguela Current.

questions.question: The type of rainfall received on the windward slopes of Mt Rwenzori.
questions.answer: Relief rainfall (orographic rainfall).

questions.question: The dry dusty wind that blows over West Africa.
questions.answer: The Harmattan.

questions.question: Why is it cold on top of Mt Kilimanjaro although it is near the Equator?
questions.answer: Because temperature falls as altitude increases — by about 1 °C for every 150 metres. Kilimanjaro is 5,895 m high, so the top is far colder than the plains below, cold enough for ice and snow.

questions.question: Give three ways in which human activities have changed the climate of Africa.
questions.answer: Cutting down forests reduces rainfall; burning bushes and using vehicles and factories releases gases that warm the earth; draining swamps reduces the moisture that goes into the air. (Overgrazing and mining also expose the soil.)

questions.question: Why do desert areas become very cold at night?
questions.answer: Deserts have clear skies and no clouds or water vapour to hold the heat. During the day the ground heats quickly, but at night the heat escapes fast into the sky, so it becomes very cold.

questions.question: A farmer in northern Uganda complains that the rains now come late and stop early. Give two possible causes and two things the community can do about it.
questions.answer: Causes: cutting down of trees and swamp drainage in the area, and wider climate change caused by global warming. Actions: plant trees (afforestation and reafforestation), protect the remaining wetlands and forests, practise agroforestry, and harvest rain water for irrigation.

questions.question: Why do people in the Sahara practise irrigation farming instead of rain-fed farming?
questions.answer: Because the desert receives less than 250 mm of rain a year, which is too little for crops. Irrigation brings water from rivers, oases or underground so that crops can grow.

questions.question: A place records a temperature of 24 °C at sea level. About what temperature would you expect 1,500 metres up the same mountain? Show your working.
Draw the map of Africa and shade the equatorial climate region.
questions.answer: Learner's map. The equatorial region should be shaded as a belt along the Equator, covering the Congo Basin and the coast of West Africa.

items.subject: Social Studies
subtopics: 6. GAME PARKS AND CARING FOR WILD ANIMALS

questions.question: Vegetation
questions.answer: Vegetation is all the plants that grow in an area — trees, shrubs, grass and herbs.

questions.question: Natural vegetation
questions.answer: Natural vegetation is vegetation that grows on its own without being planted by people.

questions.question: A game park
questions.answer: A game park is a large area of land set aside by government where wild animals are protected in their natural home.

questions.question: Poaching
questions.answer: Poaching is the illegal killing of wild animals.

questions.question: Any five types of vegetation found in Africa.
questions.answer: Any five of: equatorial forest, savannah, mangrove forest, Mediterranean vegetation, temperate grasslands (velds), desert and semi-desert vegetation, montane vegetation, swamp vegetation.

questions.question: Any three factors that influence vegetation distribution.
questions.answer: Any three of: climate, type of soil, relief/altitude, drainage, human activities.

questions.question: Any four animals found in the savannah.
questions.answer: Any four of: lions, elephants, giraffes, zebras, antelopes, buffaloes, leopards, rhinos.

questions.question: Any three game parks in Africa and the countries where they are found.
questions.answer: Any three, for example: Murchison Falls — Uganda; Serengeti — Tanzania; Maasai Mara — Kenya; Kruger — South Africa.

questions.question: The type of vegetation found in the Congo Basin.
questions.answer: Equatorial (tropical rain) forest.

questions.question: The name given to the temperate grasslands of South Africa.
questions.answer: The veld.

questions.question: One type of vegetation found along muddy sea coasts.
questions.answer: Mangrove forest.

questions.question: The vegetation zone with the largest number of big wild animals.
questions.answer: The savannah.

questions.question: One reason why deserts have very few people.
questions.answer: There is too little water and pasture; the heat is extreme and the soils are poor.

questions.question: Give four uses of vegetation to people.
questions.answer: Vegetation gives timber, firewood and charcoal; it attracts rainfall; it prevents soil erosion; it is a home for wild animals; it attracts tourists; it provides medicine, food and raw materials for industry. (Any four.)

questions.question: Why do animals live in different vegetation zones?
questions.answer: Because each animal looks for the food, water, shelter and climate that suit it. Grass eaters stay where there is grass, leaf and fruit eaters stay in the forest, and animals that hunt follow the animals they feed on. Some also move away from people.

questions.question: Give three problems faced by game parks in Africa.
questions.answer: Any three of: poaching, bush fires, drought, encroachment by farmers and herders, animal diseases, insecurity, limited funds, conflict with neighbouring communities.

questions.question: A district has cut down most of its trees for charcoal. State two effects this will have and two solutions the district should adopt.
questions.answer: Effects: rainfall will reduce and the area may face drought; the bare soil will suffer erosion and lose fertility. Solutions: start afforestation and reafforestation programmes; promote energy-saving stoves, biogas and agroforestry, and enforce laws against illegal cutting of trees.

questions.question: Why is the equatorial forest region sparsely populated although it receives plenty of rainfall?
questions.answer: Because the forest is thick and hard to clear, the soils are leached by heavy rain and are not very fertile, transport is difficult, and there are many pests and diseases such as mosquitoes and tsetse flies.

questions.question: Give two reasons why mangrove trees can grow in salty water where other trees cannot.
questions.answer: They have special stilt roots that hold them above the muddy water, and breathing roots that take in air. Their leaves and roots are also able to get rid of extra salt.

questions.question: Draw the map of Africa and shade the savannah vegetation belt north of the Equator.
questions.answer: Learner's map. The savannah belt should be shaded as a band lying between the equatorial forest and the Sahara Desert.

items.subject: Social Studies
items.topic: The People of Africa — Ethnic Groups and Settlement Patterns
subtopics: 2. THE MAIN ETHNIC GROUPS OF AFRICA
3. MOVEMENTS OF ETHNIC GROUPS INTO AND WITHIN AFRICA
5. REASONS FOR THE MIGRATION AND SETTLEMENT OF ETHNIC GROUPS
6. PROBLEMS MET DURING MOVEMENT AND SETTLEMENT

questions.question: An ethnic group
questions.answer: An ethnic group is a large group of people who share the same origin, language family, customs and way of life.

questions.question: Migration
questions.answer: Migration is the movement of people from one place to another to settle there.

questions.question: A cradle land
questions.answer: A cradle land is the original home of a group of people before they migrated.

questions.question: A settlement pattern
questions.answer: A settlement pattern is the way in which homes and villages are arranged in an area.

questions.question: Any four ethnic groups found in Africa.
questions.answer: Any four of: Bantu, Nilotics, Nilo-Hamites, Cushites, Semites (Arabs), Berbers, Pygmies (Batwa), Bushmen (San).

questions.question: Any three tribes belonging to the Bantu group.
questions.answer: Any three of: Baganda, Banyankole, Bagisu, Bakiga, Kikuyu, Chagga, Zulu, Xhosa.

questions.question: The three main settlement patterns.
questions.answer: Nucleated (clustered), dispersed (scattered) and linear.

questions.question: Any four reasons why ethnic groups migrated from their cradle lands.
questions.answer: Any four of: internal conflicts, wars, population increase, lack of enough land and water, harsh climate, expansionism, search for fertile soils and pasture, diseases and pests.

questions.question: The cradle land of the Bantu.
questions.answer: The Congo–Cameroon region of West and Central Africa.

questions.question: The cradle land of the Nilotics.
questions.answer: Bahr-el-Ghazal in southern Sudan (South Sudan).

questions.question: The ethnic group to which the Karimojong belong.
questions.answer: The Nilo-Hamites (Plain Nilotes).

questions.question: The ethnic group to which the Somali belong.
questions.answer: The Cushites (Hamites).

questions.question: The oldest known people of North Africa.
questions.answer: The Berbers.

questions.question: Give four problems that the ethnic groups met during their migrations.
questions.answer: Any four of: resistance from the indigenous people, difficulty in moving on foot over long distances, attacks by wild animals, diseases such as malaria and sleeping sickness, difficult terrain (forests, mountains, swamps, deserts), food and water shortage, harsh climate, language barriers.

questions.question: Give three positive effects and two negative effects of the ethnic migrations.
